close_reason: Implemented PathCandidates iterator in pkix-path-builder. Public API: PathCandidates<'a> (impls Iterator<Item = Result<Vec<Certificate>>>), build_path_candidates(), build_path_candidates_with_config(). Internal: replaced recursive dfs() with explicit-stack DFS (Frame struct mirrors recursion stack with anchor_checked / anchor_yielded flags + lazy candidate ranking). Iterator preserves AKI ranking (PKIX-yn3e tier ordering). Single shared budget across all next() calls (decremented per anchor check, mirroring legacy per-frame charge). After yielding Some(Err(e)), iterator becomes exhausted and subsequent next() returns None. build_path / build_path_with_config rewrote as thin wrappers over PathCandidates + a max_depth+1 probe to preserve DepthExceeded vs NoPathFound distinction. Semantic change: lost iterative-deepening shortest-first (documented in build_path rustdoc); single-pass DFS at max_depth used for both build_path and the iterator. 5 new iterator integration tests (smime retry loop with at-most-2 next() calls, full enumeration of topologically valid chains, None-after-exhaustion contract, budget bound across calls, max_depth=0 trivial chain). All 14 integration + 5 unit + dependent crate tests pass; no_std preserved (verified --no-default-features); clippy clean with -D warnings.
description:
## Why

S/MIME-in-production audit identified this as a **blocker** for the smime crate.

`build_path` returns a single `Vec<Certificate>` and is single-shot. The crate explicitly does not verify signatures during path building (`pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:11-17`, `:58`, `:346-347`); the caller is expected to feed the result to `pkix_path::validate_path`, which performs cryptographic verification.

In bridge-CA / cross-cert topologies, two distinct candidate paths can both be topologically valid (DN chains link, BasicConstraints all CA=TRUE) but only one will actually verify cryptographically. Today, when the wrong path is returned and `validate_path` rejects it with `SignatureInvalid`, **the smime caller has no API to ask for the next candidate path.** The DFS in `build_path` does internally backtrack on topological failure (`src/lib.rs:285`), but it terminates on the first topologically-valid path regardless of whether the caller can verify it.

This is the architectural seam mismatch most likely to bite S/MIME deployments. AKI heuristics (PKIX-yn3e) help by improving the *first* choice, but heuristics are preferences, not guarantees of cryptographic correctness — only re-entry into the search after a failed verify gives correctness in adversarial topologies.

## What

Add an iterator-style API alongside the existing `build_path`:

1. New public type `PathCandidates<'a>` — opaque iterator over candidate chains, leaf-first ordered. Conceptually a stream of `Result<Vec<Certificate>>` items.
2. Construction: `build_path_candidates(target, pool, anchors) -> PathCandidates<'_>` and `build_path_candidates_with_config(...)`.
3. Each `next()` resumes the DFS from where the previous chain was returned, finding the next topologically-valid path. Yields `None` when no more paths exist or the budget is exhausted.
4. Existing `build_path` becomes a thin wrapper: `PathCandidates::next()` once, return that result.
5. **Bounded enumeration**: `PathCandidates` MUST honour the same `dfs_budget` and `max_depth` constraints. The total work across all `next()` calls is bounded by the same budget — not per-call. Otherwise an attacker-controlled pool causes unbounded work.

The smime crate's expected usage:

```rust
let mut candidates = pkix_path_builder::build_path_candidates(&target, &pool, &anchors);
loop {
    match candidates.next() {
        None => return Err(NoVerifiableChain),
        Some(Err(e)) => return Err(e.into()),
        Some(Ok(chain)) => match pkix_path::validate_path(&chain, &anchors, &policy, &verifier) {
            Ok(vp) => return Ok(vp),
            Err(_) => continue, // try next candidate
        }
    }
}
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `PathCandidates` impls `Iterator<Item = Result<Vec<Certificate>>>`.
- [ ] Test fixture: pool with two same-DN cross-certs where exactly one verifies cryptographically. Iterator-based usage finds the verifying chain after at most 2 `next()` calls.
- [ ] Total budget across all `next()` calls bounded by the configured `dfs_budget`.
- [ ] `build_path` (non-iterator) behaviour unchanged — same return type, same error variants.
- [ ] no_std preserved.
- [ ] Documentation updated to recommend iterator-based usage for adversarial pools (CMS bags, etc.) and single-shot `build_path` for trusted in-house pools.

## Out of scope

- Async iterator. v1 is sync; downstream wraps if needed.
- Cross-call state externalisation (resume-from-token). The iterator carries its own state; if you drop it you start over.
- Heuristic ordering of candidates (covered by PKIX-yn3e and PKIX-rfc4158-heuristics).

## Filed as

S/MIME-in-production bar blocker. Cited in pkix-path-builder audit (this session). Audit notes this is the architectural mismatch most likely to bite S/MIME, even with AKI heuristics in place.
title: pkix-path-builder: 'next candidate path' iterator API for build-then-validate retry loops
